long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in Newark, New Jersey, Howard M. Meyers began earning money as a teenager and paid college expenses by working at a metals smelter. He transferred to New York University, completed a business degree while employed full-time and served in the United States Navy Reserve. After five years with American Metal Climax, Meyers returned to reorganise his former employer and joined investors in buying it in 1970. That company became the foundation of Quexco.

Meyers expanded through acquisitions in lead recycling, smelting, refining, mining and steel. The private holding later changed shape as former affiliates left the portfolio. Quexco now owns Bestolife, a producer of oilfield lubricants, and acquired Turkish automotive-battery manufacturer Mutlu Akü. Meyers remains Quexco's sole owner and chairman, making manufacturing the clearest current industry. His equity is an interest in the holding company; its plants, inventories, transaction values and subsidiary assets belong to the relevant companies.

Metals & Mining describes the lead-smelting, recycling and refining platform that created Meyers's fortune. Manufacturing describes Quexco's current identifiable lubricant and battery producers. Neither classification treats the holding company's transaction values or the subsidiaries' gross assets as personal wealth.

Meyers wholly owns Quexco, but Quexco and its subsidiaries own their factories, raw materials, inventories, receivables, cash, property, debt and operating assets. His personal wealth is tied to his equity in the holding company rather than the gross value or revenue of each controlled business.

Public gifts and family-foundation filings establish philanthropy but do not make foundation assets part of Meyers's personal wealth. Donated funds belong to the recipient institutions or foundation once transferred.
